reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.035:11590 (subsections 1-2 including all ten subdivisions of subsection 2) and all source notes (L. 2001 H.B. 408; Revisor footnote noting word "as" appears in original rolls at subdivision (10)), and verified all source, transcript, and subsection fingerprints. Checked catchline-versus-body discrepancy (catchline mentions conveyance/transfer while body governs local government title revestment of unused platted lots), two-foot burial buffer, 50-year non-interment condition, claim-statement termination, quiet-title procedures, and perpetual-care exclusion. Both drafted headings accurately and neutrally describe their subsections; retained both titles.

headings.title: Definition of lot owner
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 2001 H.B. 408). Defines 'lot owner' solely for section 214.035 to include the purchaser and listed successors in interest.

headings.title: Conditions and procedures to revest unused lots
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including all ten subdivisions) and section notes (L. 2001 H.B. 408; Revisor footnote noting word 'as' appears in original rolls at subdivision (10)). Covers governing bodies under section 214.010 revesting unused platted lots or ground outside burial spaces and a two-foot buffer, 50-year non-interment, personal service or publication notice, claim statements terminating proceedings, recordkeeping, quiet-title actions, prima facie abandonment, judgment recording, grave ingress/egress, perpetual-care contract exclusion, and revesting effect. Official catchline refers to conveyance/transfer, whereas archived body governs title revestment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.040:11591 (subsections 1-2) and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15261, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1079; prior revisions; Billings v. Paine, 319 S.W.2d 653 annotation confirming purchaser does not lose title when cemetery owner omits name from plat), and verified all fingerprints. Checked private/family cemetery exclusion in subsection 1 and operator record/assistance duties in subsection 2. Retained subsection 1 title and revised subsection 2 title from "Ownership records, burial logs, and location assistance" to "Lot ownership, interment records, and location assistance" for closer fidelity to statutory wording.

headings.title: Maintaining and updating cemetery plats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (RSMo 1939 § 15261, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1079; Billings v. Paine, 319 S.W.2d 653 annotation noting purchaser does not lose title when cemetery owner omits name from plat). Applies to cemetery owners other than private or family cemeteries and requires maintaining and updating a plat at an office in or within a reasonable distance of the cemetery.

headings.title: Lot ownership, interment records, and location assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (including Billings v. Paine, 319 S.W.2d 653 annotation). Covers maintaining lot-ownership and interment records (with funeral director details if known) and providing reasonable assistance to lot owners, families, and interested persons in locating lots or burial places. Revised title from "burial logs" to "Lot ownership, interment records, and location assistance" to match statutory terminology.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.132:11601 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1987 H.B. 60 §§ 2, 3, A.L. 1997 S.B. 58), and verified all fingerprints. Checked access limitations in subsection 1 (abandoned family cemetery or private burying ground, reasonable hours, usual visitation purposes), county law enforcement duty in subsection 2, and preservation of judicial disinterment authority referencing section 214.131 in subsection 3. Revised subsection 1 title from "Visitation access to landlocked family or private cemeteries" to "Limited visitation access to landlocked cemeteries" to reflect the statutory restrictions without omitting "abandoned"; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Limited visitation access to landlocked cemeteries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1987 H.B. 60 §§ 2, 3, A.L. 1997 S.B. 58). Covers reasonable ingress and egress to visit an abandoned family cemetery or private burying ground completely surrounded by private land without public access, expressly limited to reasonable hours and usual visitation purposes. Revised title to reflect the express statutory limitations and avoid dropping the "abandoned" qualifier.

headings.title: County law enforcement of visitation access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the county sheriff or chief law enforcement officer where the abandoned family cemetery or private burying ground is located to enforce subsection 1.

headings.title: Preservation of court disinterment authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Clarifies that nothing in section 214.131 or this section limits or modifies court authority in law or equity to order disinterment, removal, and reinterment in a suitable location.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.160:51074 (subsections 1-3 including all five subdivisions and paragraphs (a)-(c) of subsection 2) and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15269 through A.L. 2022 S.B. 886; prior revision 1929 § 14060), and verified all fingerprints. Checked constitutional cross-references (Art. VI § 23 and Art. IV § 15), conditional principal use solely for basic grass/weed control, fiduciary standards, and section-specific definitions. Revised subsection 1 title from "County commission investment and maintenance of trust funds" to "County trust fund investments and cemetery maintenance uses" to correct the inaccurate "maintenance of trust funds" phrasing; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: County trust fund investments and cemetery maintenance uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 15269 through A.L. 2022 S.B. 886; prior revision 1929 § 14060). Covers county commission authority under sections 214.140 to 214.180 and Missouri Constitution Art. VI § 23 and Art. IV § 15 to invest or loan cemetery trust funds, use investment managers, spend net income (and conditionally principal only for basic grass and weed maintenance when net income is insufficient) on cemeteries, and follow the trust creator's expressed wishes. Revised title to fix "maintenance of trust funds" ambiguity so cemetery maintenance use is explicit.

headings.title: Fiduciary duties and standards for investment managers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(5) and paragraphs (a)–(c)) and history note. Covers investment manager loyalty, prudent-person standard, issuer evaluation, cemetery support and expense purposes, 'appropriate consideration' factors (diversification, liquidity, projected return), and state general welfare consideration when safety and return are comparable.

headings.title: Definition of invest and investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Defines 'invest' and 'investment' specifically for section 214.160 as utilizing moneys expecting future income or capital gain.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.205:11609 (subsections 1-3) and all source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1079; section 214.500 cross-reference for St. Louis City cemetery sales; State ex rel. Nixon v. Jewell, 70 S.W.3d 465 (Mo. App. E.D. 2001) annotation holding acquisition free and clear of existing liens constituted an uncompensated taking), and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 214.090 exclusions, section 214.340 record trigger, and constitutional taking caveat affecting prior third-party obligations. Retained subsection 1 title; revised subsection 2 title to add ongoing local care and revised subsection 3 title from "Eminent domain acquisition and limits on prior liability" to "Eminent domain acquisition, public operation, and prior-liability provisions" for completeness and neutrality under Nixon v. Jewell.

headings.title: Nuisance restoration, cost assessment, and collection remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1079; cross-reference to section 214.500 for St. Louis City sales; State ex rel. Nixon v. Jewell, 70 S.W.3d 465 taking annotation). Applies to cemeteries not described in section 214.090 found violating local nuisance ordinances; authorizes restoration/maintenance, assessing true costs against responsible parties, pursuing legal/equitable/criminal remedies, and employing independent counsel for civil collection.

headings.title: Abandoned cemetery definition, dissolution, transfer, and care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1079; cross-reference to section 214.500 for St. Louis City sales; State ex rel. Nixon v. Jewell, 70 S.W.3d 465 taking annotation). Defines "abandoned cemetery" (excluding section 214.090 cemeteries, including one-year neglect or failure to keep section 214.340 records), directs attorney general dissolution of the owning corporation, vests property and endowed care funds/records in the municipality or county, and governs ongoing care using cemetery and, if needed, local funds. Revised title to include ongoing municipal/county care.

headings.title: Eminent domain acquisition, public operation, and prior-liability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes, including State ex rel. Nixon v. Jewell, 70 S.W.3d 465 (Mo. App. E.D. 2001) annotation holding county acquisition of an abandoned cemetery free and clear of existing liens constituted an uncompensated taking of the lienholder's property. Covers municipal or county eminent domain acquisition of abandoned cemeteries and related property subject to lot-owner rights, mandatory operation as a public cemetery, and statutory prior-liability disclaimer. Revised title to cover public operation and use strictly neutral "prior-liability provisions" phrasing in light of Nixon v. Jewell.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.208:11610 (subsections 1-4) and all source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 2015 H.B. 618; veto override effective date 10-16-15 referencing § 21.250), and verified all fingerprints. Checked cost-responsibility distinctions across error correction (owner), section 194.119 next-of-kin or tiered family instructions (family), and circuit court orders (as court orders), plus statutory liability immunity for authorized actions. All four drafted headings are accurate, distinct, and neutral; retained all four titles.

headings.title: Disinterment and reinterment to correct burial errors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 2015 H.B. 618; effective 10-16-15 after veto override, see § 21.250). Authorizes cemetery owners to disinter and reinter individual remains elsewhere within the cemetery at the owner's expense to correct an original burial or interment error.

headings.title: Disinterment by section 194.119 next-of-kin or family instructions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (effective 10-16-15 per veto override note). Authorizes disinterment, in-cemetery relocation, or delivery to a carrier pursuant to signed, acknowledged instructions from next-of-kin under section 194.119 or tiered surviving family majorities, with costs paid by the deceased's family.

headings.title: Court-ordered disinterment, relocation, or delivery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (effective 10-16-15 per veto override note). Authorizes disinterment, relocation, or delivery pursuant to a circuit court final order for good cause after appropriate notice and hearing, with costs paid as ordered by the court.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for authorized disinterment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes (effective 10-16-15 per veto override note). Shields cemetery owners, operators, funeral directors, funeral establishments, and other involved persons or entities from liability to family or third parties for actions taken pursuant to this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.209:11611 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 2001 H.B. 567), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 75-year non-activity reversion condition, chapter 493 publication and one-year waiting period defining a reasonable search, and settlement of later legitimate claims via an equal burial site in an equivalent location. Retained subsections 1 and 3; revised subsection 2 title from "Notice, publication, and one-year waiting period for searches" to "Reasonable search notice, publication, and one-year waiting period" for clarity.

headings.title: Abandonment and reversion after seventy-five years
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2001 H.B. 567). Provides for abandonment and reversion of burial site ownership to a private or public cemetery after 75 years without recorded activity and a reasonable search, conditioned on meeting all requirements of section 214.209.

headings.title: Reasonable search notice, publication, and one-year waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2001 H.B. 567). Defines a "reasonable search" for heirs and beneficiaries to include mailed notice to last known address, three weeks of chapter 493 newspaper publication in the county of last known address, and one year without proof of ownership before the site is deemed abandoned. Revised title to lead with the defined statutory term "Reasonable search".

headings.title: Settling later legitimate claims to used or sold sites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires settling legitimate claims presented after an abandoned site is used or sold by providing an equal burial site in an equivalent location.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.275:11619 (subsections 1-7) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343, A.L. 2001 H.B. 567, A.L. 2007 S.B. 272), and verified all fingerprints. Checked endowed/nonendowed licensing scope, unlicensed maintenance carve-out, renewal fees/assessments and suspension-expiration lifecycle, 90-day application period and prosecution bar, interim operation, and 30-day transferor/transferee rules. Revised subsection 1 title from "Cemetery operating license and local compliance requirement" to "Cemetery operating license and compliance requirements" to include state as well as county and municipal regulations; retained subsections 2 through 7.

headings.title: Cemetery operating license and compliance requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343, A.L. 2001 H.B. 567, A.L. 2007 S.B. 272). Prohibits operating an endowed care or nonendowed care cemetery without a division license and compliance with all applicable state, county, or municipal ordinances and regulations. Revised title from "local compliance requirement" to "compliance requirements" so state ordinances and regulations are not omitted.

headings.title: Permitted unlicensed maintenance and prior interment contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Clarifies that caring for or maintaining cemetery premises or fulfilling prior contractual interment obligations without a license is not unlawful.

headings.title: Written license applications and required fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires written applications on division-prescribed forms with required information and fees.

headings.title: License renewal, assessments, suspension, expiration, and reauthorization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers renewal under sections 214.270 to 214.516, section 214.340 trust report filing, $50 renewal fee plus per-disposition assessments ($10 endowed / $6 nonendowed caps), renewal notices and address updates, automatic suspension after three months, nine-month reinstatement, expiration, and reauthorization under the original license number.

headings.title: Application decision period and prosecution limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires granting or denying applications within 90 days of filing and bars initiating prosecution against an applicant unless denial and owner notification are shown.

headings.title: Interim operation while completed application is pending
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Authorizes an applicant who has filed a completed application as defined by rule to operate the business until the division acts.

headings.title: License return and transferee application on cemetery transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires transferors to return licenses within 30 days after sale or transfer of ownership or control, and prospective purchasers or transferees to apply at least 30 days beforehand in compliance with sections 214.270 to 214.516.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.276:48387 (subsections 1-5 including all 15 subdivisions of subsection 2) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046), and verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 621 AHC procedures, chapter 195 and section 324.012 cross-references, section 214.410(4) administrative penalties, three-year post-revocation bar, section 621.045 settlement agreements, and preservation of other chapter remedies. Revised subsection 1 title from "Refusal to issue or renew licenses and appeal notice" to "Refusal to issue or renew licenses and review notice"; retained subsections 2 through 5.

headings.title: Refusal to issue or renew licenses and review notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Authorizes refusing to issue or renew licenses under sections 214.270 to 214.516 for subsection 2 causes, with written reasons and notice of the right to file a chapter 621 complaint with the administrative hearing commission. Revised "appeal notice" to "review notice" to reflect chapter 621 AHC complaint review without confusion with subsection 2 disciplinary complaints.

headings.title: Disciplinary complaints and enumerated causes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including all fifteen subdivisions) and history note. Authorizes division complaints with the administrative hearing commission under chapter 621 against license holders or persons failing to surrender licenses, enumerating 15 causes including chapter 195 substance impairment, section 324.012 directly related criminal offenses, fraud, misconduct, regulatory violations, and undue influence in sales.

headings.title: Hearing procedures, disciplinary sanctions, and revocation waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Governs chapter 621 proceedings, available sanctions upon findings (censure, probation up to five years, suspension, revocation, or section 214.410(4) penalties), and a three-year bar on issuing a new license after revocation to the owner, operator, or owner-controlled corporation.

headings.title: Disciplinary consent and settlement agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes settling subsection 2 and 3 disputes under section 621.045 procedures, allowing any discipline or section 214.410(4) penalty within the agreement.

headings.title: Preservation of other chapter remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. States that using section 214.276 procedures does not preclude applying any other remedy provided by chapter 214.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.277:11621 (subsections 1-2 including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed source discrepancy noted by drafter: official catchline references "venue", whereas archived body specifies only "a court of general jurisdiction" without a venue clause; neither title invents venue language. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Court injunctions and restraining orders on division application
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 343, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Authorizes a court of general jurisdiction, upon division application and meeting the necessary burden, to enjoin unlicensed regulated acts or licensed practices presenting a substantial probability of serious danger. Official catchline mentions 'venue', though the archived body specifies only a court of general jurisdiction without a venue clause.

headings.title: Cumulative and concurrent nature of injunctive actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Clarifies that actions under this section are in addition to, not in lieu of, chapter penalties and may be brought concurrently with other chapter enforcement actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.280:11622 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 4, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 § 214.280 subsecs. 1, 2, A.L. 2009 S.B. 296), and verified all fingerprints. Checked historical August 28, 1994 election timing, section 214.270(16) and section 193.265 cross-references, existing nonendowed fee exemption, and endowed-to-nonendowed conversion rules and prior contract fulfillment. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Election of endowed or nonendowed status and filing fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 4, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496, A.L. 2009 S.B. 296). Covers existing-cemetery election deadlines following August 28, 1994 (referencing section 214.270(16)), 90-day election for newly established cemeteries, division-set filing fees deposited in the section 193.265 endowed care cemetery audit fund, and the fee exemption for existing nonendowed cemeteries.

headings.title: Conversion from endowed to nonendowed status and prior contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes division rules for conditions and procedures when an endowed care cemetery elects to operate as nonendowed, and directs the division to make every effort to require fulfillment of prior service contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.282:11623 (subsections 1-2 including subdivisions (1)-(6)) and all source notes (L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Revisor footnote noting word "sections" appears in original rolls at subdivision (4)), and verified all fingerprints. Checked scope distinction between subsection 1 ("Each contract") and subsection 2 ("cemetery prearranged contract") and exact cross-references. Revised subsection 1 title from "Required contract terms to avoid voidability" to "Contract requirements to avoid voidability" to encompass writing and operator-licensing conditions; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Contract requirements to avoid voidability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(6)) and section notes (L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Revisor footnote noting word "sections" appears in original rolls at subdivision (4)). Makes cemetery service and merchandise/space contracts voidable by the purchaser and unenforceable unless six conditions are met, including writing, compliant licensed operator, identification of items/parties/operator, trustee or escrow agent details under section 214.320, 214.330, or 214.387 if applicable, and cancellation grounds. Revised "Required contract terms" to "Contract requirements" because subdivisions (1) and (2) cover written form and operator licensing compliance, not merely contract terms.

headings.title: Purchaser recovery for noncompliant prearranged contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers recovery of payments, ten percent annual interest, and reasonable collection costs including attorneys' fees by the purchaser or legal representative if a cemetery prearranged contract does not substantially comply with this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.283:11624 (subsections 1-2 including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 4, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 § 214.280 subsec. 3, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked family burial ground exclusion, October 1, 2010 / 30-day notice rules, no-fee/no-penalty and licensing-preservation clauses, public cemetery registry copy fees, chapter 327 surveyor filings, and voluntary submissions. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Notification of burial lands and licensing preservation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 4, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Requires persons, entities, and political subdivisions holding burial real estate (excluding family burial grounds) to notify the office of endowed care cemeteries before October 1, 2010 or within 30 days of acquisition or office notice, with no fee or penalty and without exempting cemetery licensing.

headings.title: Public cemetery registry and surveyor or voluntary filings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Covers maintaining a public cemetery registry with optional copy fees, mandatory no-fee location statements by chapter 327 licensed surveyors who locate unregistered cemeteries, and voluntary no-fee submissions by others.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.310:11627 (subsections 1-3) and all source notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 5 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Revisor footnote noting word "a" appears in original rolls at subsection 3 "an* adequately staffed office"), and verified all fingerprints. Checked tiered initial deposit minimums ($25,000/$5,000), $30,000 surety bond alternative and dissolution petition, additions to existing endowed care cemeteries, and premises signage or weatherproof notice rules. Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Initial endowed care trust deposit and surety bond option
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 5 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Requires creating an endowed care trust fund with $25,000 or $5,000 minimum deposits based on annual burials (over 100 vs 100 or less), permits a $30,000 surety bond alternative with capped liability, and allows petitioning the administrator to dissolve the bond once more than $25,000 is accumulated and maintained.

headings.title: Additions to existing endowed care cemeteries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Specifies that constructing a mausoleum, lawn crypt, columbarium, or crematorium as part of an existing endowed care cemetery is not establishing a new cemetery under this section.

headings.title: Premises signage when no staffed in-county office exists
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (including Revisor footnote noting word 'a' appears in original rolls at 'an* adequately staffed office'). Requires prominent signage displaying operator contact details (and local agent or nearby office within ten miles if operator resides outside the county), permitting a weatherproof notice where local sign ordinances impose specifications.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.320:11628 (subsections 1-5 including subdivisions (1)-(4) of subsection 1) and all source notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 7 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Revisor footnote noting word "a" appears in original rolls at subsection 3 "an* escrow account"; Rosebrough Monument Co. v. Memorial Park Cemetery, 736 F.2d 441 (8th Cir. 1984) annotation), and verified all fingerprints. Checked monthly deposit schedules, initial-deposit recoupment rule, section 214.340/214.387 audit access, and chapter 436 exemption with anti-evasion pricing ban. Revised subsection 4 title from "Compliance required before representing endowed care status" to "Compliance required to operate or represent endowed care" to capture both prohibited acts; retained subsections 1, 2, 3, and 5.

headings.title: Minimum monthly trust fund deposits by burial space type
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(4)) and section notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 7 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Rosebrough Monument Co., 736 F.2d 441 annotation regarding third-party monument installers). Sets minimum monthly deposits for fully paid grave spaces, community mausoleum crypts/niches, garden mausoleum crypts/niches, and lawn crypts.

headings.title: Reduced deposits while recouping operator's initial deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Allows operators who funded the initial trust deposit under sections 214.270 to 214.410 from their own funds to deposit half the minimums in subdivisions (1) and (2) of subsection 1 until recouped, after which all four minimums apply.

headings.title: Annual trust reports and division record inspections or audits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (including Revisor footnote noting word 'a' appears in original rolls at 'an* escrow account'). Covers filing annual reports under section 214.340 and making necessary cemetery, trust fund, and section 214.387 escrow/financial institution records available to the division at reasonable times.

headings.title: Compliance required to operate or represent endowed care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes. Prohibits operating or representing to the public that a cemetery provides endowed care unless compliant with sections 214.270 to 214.410. Revised title to cover both operating and representing endowed care status.

headings.title: Chapter 436 exemption and prohibition on evasive pricing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section notes. Exempts cemetery operators from chapter 436 for listed cemetery service and merchandise/space sales, while prohibiting adjusting or setting prices with intent to evade chapter 214 trusting or escrow provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.330:11630 (subsections 1-11 including all subdivisions) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 8 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked Missouri trustee and record-access rules, chapters 456 and 469 rules and exclusions (sections 469.405, 469.411, 456.1-108, 456.4-414), escrow account $350,000 cap and exact archived phrase "accounting for an investment of moneys" in subsection 5(2), trust agreement 30-day review/deemed approval/subsequent disapproval, commingling, and jurisdiction/service-of-process consent. Revised subsection 4 title from "Trustee accounting duties and operator care responsibilities" to "Trustee duties, exclusions, and operator care responsibilities"; retained the remaining ten headings.

headings.title: Trust fund establishment, Missouri trustees, records, and jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 8 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Covers permanently setting aside endowed care funds in trust, Missouri-authorized financial institution trustees and contact disclosure, in-state or 15-business-day electronic record availability, and controlling Missouri law and court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Chapters 456 and 469 trust administration and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(8)) and history note. Applies Missouri trust law (chapters 456 and 469) without operator modification and establishes eight specific rules: excluding section 469.405, barring principal distributions except under section 469.411 unitrust elections, barring section 456.1-108 jurisdiction transfers, irrevocability, barring section 456.4-414 termination, operator-only unitrust elections, excluding insurance contracts as investments, and 60-day post-fiscal-year income distribution or rollover to principal.

headings.title: Restricted use of distributed trust income
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Obligates cemetery operators to apply distributed income solely for care and maintenance of the designated endowed care section.

headings.title: Trustee duties, exclusions, and operator care responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Assigns trust recordkeeping, accounting, and investment duties to the trustee while expressly excluding trustee responsibility for cemetery care, maintenance, operation, expenditure oversight, or environmental compliance, leaving physical care to the cemetery operator. Revised title from "Trustee accounting duties..." to reflect broader trustee duties and express exclusions.

headings.title: Escrow account alternative, interest distributions, and escrow agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note. Permits insured Missouri escrow accounts up to $350,000 (unless division approves otherwise for good cause), sets six-month post-calendar-year interest distribution or principal rollover, states operator care and accounting duties (retaining exact source phrase 'accounting for an investment of moneys') and administrator non-responsibility, and allows division approval of qualified escrow agents.

headings.title: Operator accountability to burial space owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. States that the cemetery operator is accountable to burial space owners for compliance with sections 214.270 to 214.410.

headings.title: Submission and review of endowed care trust agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires submitting trust fund agreements (excluding escrow accounts) to the office of endowed care cemeteries for review, written approval or disapproval, and required compliance changes.

headings.title: Advance filing of trust agreement amendments or revisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Imposes a continuing duty to file any trust agreement changes, amendments, or revisions for prior approval at least 30 days before their effective date.

headings.title: Deemed approval after thirty days and subsequent disapproval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Deems submitted agreements or changes approved if not disapproved within 30 days, while preserving office authority to review and disapprove noncompliant agreements at any time with written notice to operator and trustee within ten days.

headings.title: Commingling endowed care funds across cemeteries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Permits commingling trust or escrow funds across endowed care cemeteries provided the operator and trustee maintain adequate per-cemetery accounting of disbursements, contributions, and income.

headings.title: Trustee and escrow agent jurisdiction and service-of-process consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Establishes personal submission to Missouri courts and the office upon accepting funds, and requires prior written consent to jurisdiction and secretary-of-state service of process if no in-state agent is designated.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.335:11631 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked uniform 20-cent/sq-in installation contribution cap and August 28, 1990 contract cutoff in subsection 1, and five-year deficiency cure, section 214.330/214.410 consequences, and investment-fluctuation exclusion from "deficiency" in subsection 2. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Memorial or monument installation contributions to care funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Permits endowed care cemeteries to require uniform installation contributions up to twenty cents per square inch of base area regardless of installer, governed by sections 214.270 to 214.410 for post-August 28, 1990 contracts and prior law for earlier contracts.

headings.title: Curing trust fund deficiencies and definition of deficiency
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires five-year annual twenty-percent deficiency cure deposits and reporting, bars endowed care representation if uncured under section 214.330 while preserving trust use and section 214.410/civil/regulatory exposure, and defines 'deficiency' to exclude investment value fluctuations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.340:11632 (subsections 1-4 including subdivisions (1)-(9) of subsection 1 and subdivisions (1)-(2) of subsection 4) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 9 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Explicitly audited source omissions/wording: subsection 2 mandates sworn officer certification of subdivisions (1)-(7) by the trustee and subdivision (8) by the cemetery operator while omitting subdivision (9) (total and developed acreage), and subsection 4(1) uses archived phrase "by purchase designation"; retained source text faithfully without inventing corrections. Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Retention and required contents of trust fund reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(9)) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 9 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Requires endowed care cemetery operators to retain seven years of trust operation reports at an in-cemetery or nearby office and specifies nine required disclosures.

headings.title: Sworn certifications by trustee and cemetery operator officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires sworn certification of subdivisions (1)–(7) by a trustee corporate officer and subdivision (8) by a cemetery operator officer, both subject to false-affidavit penalties; retains archived text as written (subdivision (9) is not listed in the certification sentence).

headings.title: Report placement deadline and filing for license renewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires placing the report in the cemetery's office within 90 days after the trust's fiscal year closes and filing a copy with the division of professional registration as a license renewal condition under section 214.275(4).

headings.title: Accompanying report for section 214.387 escrow or trust accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Requires operators with section 214.387 accounts to file with the subsection 1 report the total face value of deferred-delivery contracts (archived wording "by purchase designation") and the amount on deposit (plus account number for escrow accounts).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.345:11633 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked prospective-purchaser plain-language endowed/nonendowed disclosures referencing section 214.340 and public right to request a copy of the section 214.340(1) annual report for retention. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Written endowed or nonendowed care disclosures to prospective purchasers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Requires operators negotiating burial space sales to give prospective owners a plain-language written statement disclosing endowed care status and section 214.340 report availability, or stating election not to establish an endowed care trust fund for nonendowed cemeteries or sections.

headings.title: Public access to annual trust fund reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires endowed care cemetery operators, upon request, to give the public for retention a copy of the annual report prepared under section 214.340(1).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.367:11637 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 § 214.360 subsec. 4, A.L. 2001 H.B. 567, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 30-day advance notice and chapter 610 confidentiality until sale effectuation, division audit/waiver powers, completion absent disapproval within 30 days with preserved division/AG remedies, and prospective-purchaser audit access (retaining archived phrasing "of endowed or unendowed cemetery" in subsection 3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Advance confidential notice of cemetery sale, transfer, or termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 § 214.360 subsec. 4, A.L. 2001 H.B. 567, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Requires 30-day prior written notice before disposing of a majority of assets/ownership or terminating business, makes notice exempt from chapter 610 until sale effectuation, authorizes division audit/review of trust or escrow plans, and allows waiving or shortening notice.

headings.title: Completing transactions absent disapproval and preserved remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits completing the sale, transfer, or cessation if not disapproved within 30 days of division receipt, without restricting other division or attorney general rights or remedies.

headings.title: Prospective purchaser audit access and division continuation notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits prospective purchasers or transferees of endowed or unendowed cemeteries, with operator written consent, to obtain the most recent division audit or inspection report, and requires the division to state within 30 days whether cemetery operation and representation may continue.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.370:11638 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 10), and verified all fingerprints. Checked nonendowed cemetery operator applicability, 50-foot-readable office signage, specified printed notices on sales and advertising materials, and pre-sale purchaser disclosure. Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Applicability to nonendowed cemetery operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 538 § 10). Requires every operator of a nonendowed cemetery to comply with section 214.370.

headings.title: Conspicuous office signage stating nonendowed status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires posting a legible sign reading 'This is a nonendowed cemetery.' readable from fifty feet in every office conducting sales of nonendowed burial space.

headings.title: Printed notices on sales materials and pre-sale disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires printing or stamping the nonendowed statement in specified type at the head of contracts, deeds, statements, letterheads, and advertising, and informing purchasers before any sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.385:11640 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 § 214.385 subsecs. 1, 2(a) merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2009 S.B. 296), and verified all fingerprints. Checked reasonable-time replacement of moved markers/memorials/monuments by operators or authorized persons and reasonable-time delivery of paid burial merchandise or valid warehouse receipts. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Timely replacement of moved grave markers or monuments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1079, A.L. 1994 S.B. 496 merged with S.B. 701, A.L. 2009 S.B. 296). Requires operators or other authorized persons who move a grave marker, memorial, or monument for any reason to return it to its original position within a reasonable time.

headings.title: Delivery of paid burial merchandise or warehouse receipts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires timely delivery of burial merchandise once paid in full, allowing compliance via a valid warehouse receipt presentable later for actual delivery.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.387:11641 (subsections 1-8 including all subdivisions of subsections 3, 4, and 6) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 214.385 carve-out, 80% deposit / 60-day deferral rules, escrow versus trust requirements and section 214.330 approval procedures, performance/cancellation certificates, cancellation refunds and public-assistance waivers (retaining archived phrasing "subdivision (1) of this section" in subsection 6(2)), post-death exemption, and August 28, 2010 applicability date. Retained all eight drafted headings.

headings.title: Scope for prearranged sales outside section 214.385
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Governs all sales of prearranged burial merchandise and services except sales made pursuant to section 214.385.

headings.title: Deferred delivery, escrow or trust deposits, and withdrawal limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows deferring merchandise/warehouse-receipt delivery (referencing section 214.385) or service performance upon purchaser written instructions if at least 80% of the purchase price (after up to 20% sales/administrative costs) is deposited within 60 days, held until delivery/performance/cancellation subject to division audit and maintenance charges, with restricted withdrawals.

headings.title: Requirements for prearranged-contract escrow arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history note. Sets rules for independent Missouri escrow agents, five-business-day record access, open-record agent info, insured Missouri depository accounts, section 214.330 agreement approval, separate accounts per contract, and optional division form escrow agreement rules.

headings.title: Requirements for prearranged-contract trusts and commingling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(6)) and history note. Covers Missouri-authorized financial institution trustees (with office approval for foreign institutions), record access, chapter 469 prudent-investor standard barring term insurance products, individual-contract commingling, section 214.330 instrument approval, and investment commingling across unrelated operators with accounting.

headings.title: Escrow income distributions and performance or cancellation certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs net escrow income to the cemetery operator and requires office-approved forms—signed certificate of performance by operator, or certificate of cancellation by operator and purchaser—for all other trust and escrow distributions.

headings.title: Cancellation, refunds, public-assistance waivers, and creditor exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history note. Covers 80%-refund cancellation before disposition/delivery and operator's half of trust interest, irrevocable written waivers for chapter 208 or other public assistance (retaining archived phrase 'subdivision (1) of this section'), 30-day full-refund cancellation, noncancellable merchandise production orders, and exemption from operator creditors.

headings.title: Exemption for post-death burial merchandise contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Exempts burial merchandise sold under contracts entered into after the intended individual's death from section 214.387 trusting or escrow requirements.

headings.title: Applicability to agreements entered after August 28, 2010
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Specifies that section 214.387 applies to all agreements entered into after August 28, 2010.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.389:11642 (subsections 1-6) and history note (L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked distribution-suspension grounds and deficiency definition (referencing sections 214.320, 214.335(1), and 214.330 while excluding investment fluctuations), 14-day notice and 60-day cure period, trustee/escrow liability exemption, reinstatement, and chapter 536 / August 28, 2010 nonseverability. Explicitly audited source discrepancy in subsection 4 ("Failure of a person whose license was suspended" within this distribution-suspension appeal provision); retained exact archived text without correction and retained all six drafted headings.

headings.title: Grounds to suspend distributions and deficiency definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Authorizes directing suspension of distributions for lacking an active license, failing to file an annual report, or an uncured audit deficiency under section 214.330; defines 'deficiency' by reference to sections 214.320, 214.335(1), and 214.330 while excluding investment value fluctuations.

headings.title: Violation notice, sixty-day cure period, suspension, and stays
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires 14-day written violation notice, provides a 60-day cure period before ordering suspension, converts suspended distributions into principal credited against the deficiency absent appeal, and allows requesting a stay or necessary-expense disbursements during an appeal.

headings.title: Compliance and liability exemption for trustees and escrow agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs immediate suspension upon receiving a division order and exempts trustees, financial institutions, and escrow agents from liability for complying.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission appeals of suspension orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits appeals to the administrative hearing commission within 30 days of certified-mail suspension notice for a chapter 621 hearing, with waiver on failure to notify (retains exact archived wording 'person whose license was suspended' within this distribution-suspension section).

headings.title: Applying to reinstate suspended distributions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Allows cemetery operators to apply for reinstatement of distributions upon showing deficiencies or problems are cured or compliance is restored.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Authorizes implementing rules under chapter 536 and section 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause voiding post-August 28, 2010 rules and rulemaking authority if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.392:50056 (subsections 1-2 including subdivisions (1)-(6) and paragraphs (a)-(c) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 26 merged with S.B. 53 & 60), and verified all fingerprints. Checked division enforcement/audit duties, inmate-care conveyance authority, fee deposits to the section 193.265 audit fund, section 214.283 registry rulemaking, and chapter 536 / August 28, 2001 nonseverability clause. Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Division regulatory duties, powers, fees, and rulemaking topics
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(6) and paragraphs (a)–(c)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 496 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 26 merged with S.B. 53 & 60). Covers prosecution recommendations, staffing, conveying authority for local use of corrections inmates on abandoned cemeteries, management functions, compliance audits, and permissive rulemaking for fees (deposited in the section 193.265 fund), inspections/audits, and the section 214.283 registry.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause voiding post-August 28, 2001 rules and rulemaking authority if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.410:11646 (subsections 1-4) and all source notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 15 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17), and verified all fingerprints. Checked party scope across all four subsections (cemetery operators in subsections 1-2, trustees in subsection 3, any person in subsection 4), archived wording "This section" in the subsection 2 non-selling cemetery exemption, exclusive division-of-finance and AG enforcement under chapters 361-362, and section 214.387 appearing in subsection 2 but not subsection 4. Revised subsection 1 title to add "Operator" for party clarity; retained subsections 2, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Operator misdemeanor penalty for unspecified willful violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section notes (L. 1961 p. 538 § 15 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17). Makes willful violations by a cemetery operator of sections 214.270 to 214.410 without another prescribed penalty a misdemeanor punishable by fine up to $500, confinement up to six months, or both. Revised title to specify "Operator" for clear party distinction from trustees in subsection 3 and any person in subsection 4.

headings.title: Class E felony violations and non-selling cemetery exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (effective 1-01-17). Makes willful violations of sections 214.320, 214.330, 214.335, 214.340, 214.360, 214.385, or 214.387 a class E felony (up to $10,000 fine, five years confinement, or both), and states 'This section' does not apply to cemeteries or cemetery associations that do not sell lots.

headings.title: Trustee banking penalties and exclusive enforcement authorities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (effective 1-01-17). Treats willful trustee violations of sections 214.270 to 214.410 as unsafe and unsound banking practices penalized under chapters 361 and 362, enforced exclusively by the Missouri division of finance for state-chartered institutions and the attorney general for federally chartered institutions.

headings.title: Administrative penalties, hearing opportunity, and fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes (effective 1-01-17). Authorizes division administrative penalties up to $5,000 per violation (each continuing day separate) against any person for willful violations of six listed sections (214.320, 214.330, 214.335, 214.340, 214.360, or 214.385—noting 214.387 is listed in subsection 2 but not here) or any division rule, regulation, or order, after a hearing opportunity, with receipts deposited in the section 193.265 audit fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 214.550:11655 (subsections 1-4 including subdivisions (1)-(4) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1148, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked IRC Section 501(c) religious cemetery definition, adjacency requirement to a church or regular place of worship, operator maintenance and cremains recordkeeping (including Social Security numbers), and post-dissolution transfer of records to municipal clerk or county recorder. Revised subsection 2 title from "Authority to establish scatter gardens at religious cemeteries" to "Establishing scatter gardens at qualifying religious cemeteries" to preserve the adjacency qualification; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Definitions for religious cemetery scatter gardens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(4)) and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1148, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Defines 'cremains', 'operator', 'religious cemetery' (including IRC Section 501(c) qualification), and 'scatter garden' for section 214.550.

headings.title: Establishing scatter gardens at qualifying religious cemeteries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1148, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Authorizes an operator of a religious cemetery adjacent to a church building or other building regularly used as a place of worship to establish a scatter garden for human cremains. Revised title to add "qualifying" so the adjacency condition is not over-generalized.

headings.title: Maintenance, supervision, cost responsibility, and cremains records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires religious cemetery operators with scatter gardens to maintain, protect, and supervise the garden at their own cost and keep records of scattered cremains including name, death date, Social Security number, and scattering date.

headings.title: Duration of maintenance and transfer of records upon dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires maintaining the scatter garden while the operator exists and transferring all cremains records upon dissolution to the municipal clerk, or to the county recorder in unincorporated areas.
